s01.en.heard: Why would a young boy walk 20 kilometers across Ethiopia every Sunday evening just to attend primary school?

s02.en.heard: Gebisa Ejeta was born in Wollonkomi, to Oromo parents, encouraged constantly by his mother to pursue education.

s03.en.heard: He intended to study engineering, but his mother convinced him he could accomplish more working in agriculture.

s04.en.heard: After studying at Haramaya University, Ejeta earned his doctorate in plant breeding from Purdue University in 1978.

s05.en.heard: He went to work in rain-starved Northern Sudan, researching sorghum crops for five straight years.

s06.en.heard: His drought tolerant hybrid produced yields up to 150% higher, covering 1 million acres in Sudan yearly.

s07.en.heard: At Purdue, he developed a mechanism to stop parasitic striga weeds from attacking sorghum crops.

s08.en.heard: In 1994, 8 tons of his resistant seeds were distributed to 12 African nations.

s09.en.heard: Farmers planting them reported crop yields up to four times larger than traditional harvests.

s10.en.heard: President Biden awarded this scientist from Wlamcaney the National Medal of Science in 2023.
